lines.trans: Chef, forgive us, I really did not mean to.
And I do not care at all anymore.
We have nothing at all to feed the guests in the hall.
It is all over, our restaurant is finished.
That means I will not have to tolerate you anymore.
And you too, I am going home right now.
There is nothing to feed the guests, we must do something fast.
Do not think that we are skimping on electricity.
We are the true elite of Moscow's restaurant business.
We are trying to create a special warm atmosphere here.
Dima, and when will they finally bring us food?
Do I need to invest money in the restaurant first?

examples.trans: We're in business.

meanings.en: to try, to attempt, to make an effort
meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to try, to attempt', paired with 'попытаться'.

examples.text: Я пыталась!
examples.trans: I tried!

examples.text: Он пытался объяснить ситуацию.
examples.trans: He tried to explain the situation.

examples.text: Пыталась? С бутылкой вина в руке?
examples.trans: You tried? With a bottle of wine in your hand?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'оздавать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to create, cause', paired with 'создать'.

examples.text: Мы пытаемся создавать тут особую тёплую обстановку.
examples.trans: We are trying to create a special warm atmosphere here.

examples.text: Ты создаешь нам лишние проблемы.
examples.trans: You create unnecessary problems for us.

examples.text: Художник создает новую картину.
examples.trans: The artist creates a new painting.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'here', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Что ты тут стоишь и слушаешь?
examples.trans: Why are you standing here listening?

examples.text: Ты от кого тут сейчас прячешься, Макс?
examples.trans: Who are you hiding from right here, Max?

examples.text: Мне надо срочно проверить тут электричество.
examples.trans: I need to urgently check the electricity here.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('special, particular').

examples.text: Да мы сегодня не особо спешим.
examples.trans: We are not in much of a hurry today.

examples.text: Мы пытаемся создавать тут особую тёплую обстановку.
examples.trans: We are trying to create a special warm atmosphere here.

examples.text: У нас особый подход к каждому нашему гостю.
examples.trans: We have a special approach to every guest of ours.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('warm').

examples.text: Мы пытаемся создавать тут особую тёплую обстановку.
examples.trans: We are trying to create a special warm atmosphere here.

examples.text: Дома ведь такие тёплые и уютные стены.
examples.trans: At home the walls are so warm and cozy.

examples.text: А где твои тёплые перчатки?
examples.trans: And where are your warm gloves?

meanings.note: Prefix 'об-' ('around, about') marks encirclement or comprehensive action (stem 'становка'). Common feminine noun meaning 'atmosphere / setting' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Мы пытаемся создавать тут особую тёплую обстановку.
examples.trans: We are trying to create a special warm atmosphere here.

examples.text: На кухне ресторана всегда есть обстановка.
examples.trans: In the restaurant kitchen there is always atmosphere.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'when', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Здесь всегда продукты самого высокого качества.
examples.trans: There are always products of the highest quality here.

examples.text: Ты от кого тут сейчас прячешься, Макс?
examples.trans: Who are you hiding from right here, Max?

examples.text: Да я вовсе ни от кого не прячусь.
examples.trans: I am not hiding from anyone at all.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'конец').

examples.text: Дима, а когда нам наконец еду принесут?
examples.trans: Dima, and when will they finally bring us food?

examples.text: О, наконец тепло!
examples.trans: Oh, it's warm at last!

examples.text: Наконец мы дома.
examples.trans: We are finally home.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'food' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Катя, ты случайно недавно не поправилась?
examples.trans: Katya, did you happen to gain weight recently?

examples.text: Ой, плохая еда?
examples.trans: Oh, bad food?

examples.text: В этом ресторане всегда свежая еда.
examples.trans: There is always fresh food in this restaurant.

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'нести'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to bring (carrying)', paired with 'приносить'.

examples.text: Макс, принеси мне то, сделай мне это.
examples.trans: Max, bring me that, do this for me.

examples.text: Дима, а когда нам наконец еду принесут?
examples.trans: Dima, and when will they finally bring us food?

examples.text: Что ты в квартиру принёс?
examples.trans: What did you bring into the flat?

meanings.en: it is necessary, one needs to
meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Конечно, нашему ресторану нужен хороший хозяин.
examples.trans: Of course, our restaurant needs a good owner.

examples.text: Мне новые отношения сейчас совсем не нужны.
examples.trans: I do not need a new relationship at all right now.

examples.text: Мне новые отношения не нужны.
examples.trans: I do not need a new relationship.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'начала').

examples.text: Мне нужно сначала деньги в ресторан вложить?
examples.trans: Do I need to invest money in the restaurant first?

examples.text: Сначала они там грубили, оскорбляли.
examples.trans: First they were rude and insulting over there.

examples.text: Давай начнём всё сначала.
examples.trans: Let's start everything from the beginning.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'money' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Там были все мои деньги!
examples.trans: All my money was in there!

examples.text: Там были все мои деньги, понимаешь?
examples.trans: All my money was in there, do you understand?

examples.text: Деньги были на наш второй этаж.
examples.trans: The money was for our second floor.

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to invest / put in', paired with 'вкладывать'.

examples.text: Этот человек хочет вложить в нас деньги.
examples.trans: This man wants to invest money in us.

examples.text: Мне нужно сначала деньги в ресторан вложить?
examples.trans: Do I need to invest money in the restaurant first?

examples.text: Вложи деньги в бизнес.
examples.trans: Invest the money in a business.
